articles.title: To Read a 2,000-Year-Old Library, Scientists Burned Their Own Scrolls First
articles.summary: A volcano charred an entire Roman library in 79 C.E., leaving 1,800 scrolls too fragile to open. Now a scientist has found that lead in ancient ink could let X-rays read the lost words — without touching the scrolls.

articles.title: Quantum Computer Simulates the Moment Matter 'Pops Into Existence'
articles.summary: Physicists used 13 trapped ions to recreate string breaking — a process where pulling particles apart creates new ones. It's one of the first lab demonstrations of physics normally seen only in the Big Bang or particle colliders.

articles.title: NASA's PRIMA Telescope Will Hunt for What JWST Can't See
articles.summary: NASA is moving ahead with PRIMA, a $1.2 billion telescope designed to observe far-infrared light — wavelengths beyond JWST's reach. Launching as early as 2033, it could reveal how planets form and how black holes grow.
